sources.entry: aicontainer by stefanoginella - Sandboxed devcontainer for running Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode in bypass / auto-approve mode.

summary.one_liner: aicontainer is a devcontainer setup that runs Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode in bypass/auto-approve mode inside a sandbox so a compromised dependency cannot reach the real home directory, SSH keys, or host credentials.
summary.what_it_does: The project directory is the only writable host path, mounted at /workspace; the host home, ~/.ssh, and the SSH agent are not mounted into the container. Host Git and tool preferences are copied through a networkless sanitizer that keeps only allowlisted fields and strips credentials, hooks, statusLine, and Git credential helpers, aliases, and includes. A networkless credential bridge shares login tokens between projects while transcripts, memory, and settings stay per project. The aic CLI validates managed files and the resolved Compose model before Docker starts, and a digest-pinned socket proxy gives no Docker object access by default, with read or read-write as explicit opt-ins. Cloud-metadata and link-local addresses are always blocked, an outbound network allowlist is optional, and a shared PreToolUse hook refuses obvious .env reads, curl-pipe-to-shell, and writes to sandbox control files across all three tools.
use_cases: run Claude Code in auto-approve mode safely
sandbox AI coding agents from host secrets
isolate AI coding CLIs per project
keep .env files and SSH keys away from an AI agent
use Codex and OpenCode in a devcontainer
share AI tool logins across multiple projects
notable: Filesystem isolation: only the project directory is writable from the host, with host home and SSH agent kept out of the container
Three explicit Docker-access modes, with no Docker object access by default
Sanitized copy of host Git and tool config, with credentials and hooks stripped
Shared PreToolUse guardrail hook across Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode
Compose model validated by aic before Docker starts
caveats: Outbound network is mostly open by default; the allowlist is an opt-in
.env block is best-effort only, so unrecoverable secrets should stay out of the project directory
Opening an unknown repo's .devcontainer directly in VS Code bypasses aic validation; README advises running aic init --force and reviewing first
